item.title: Stephen Colbert Makes Surprise Michigan Public Access Appearance After ‘Late Show’ Farewell
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, where we dive into the latest trending topics. Today, we're talking about Stephen Colbert's surprise appearance on a public access show in Michigan, just days after wrapping up his 11-year run on The Late Show.
[Short music transition]
Host: Colbert guest-hosted an episode of "Only in Monroe" on Friday, May 22nd, a show he had previously appeared on in 2015. He even foreshadowed his return during his Late Show finale, joking that he'd likely end up back on the small public access show. And that's exactly what happened.
[Short music transition]
Host: The episode was a love letter to Michigan local culture, with Jack White serving as volunteer musical director and Jeff Daniels making a unique sandwich. Steve Buscemi even appeared in a hilarious public service announcement, clarifying that he has no connection to a Michigan pizza chain that shares his name.
[Short music transition]
Host: The episode ended with Colbert, White, and Daniels destroying the set and burning it in a flaming dumpster, with Eminem giving the all-clear via video. It was a wild and entertaining ride, and a perfect way for Colbert to cap off his post-Late Show era.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one.
